Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Senior Manager Tax Reporting

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. Amgen's Tax Reporting group is part of a world-class tax department that provides global tax planning, transfer pricing, tax reporting, and tax audit defense for the Company. The Tax Reporting team is a critical function providing advice on tax accounting, tax rate forecasting, and the financial statement tax provision process. The group works closely with Finance, Accounting, Treasury, Tax Planning, Regional Tax, Transfer Pricing, and Tax Audit teams to prepare Amgen's financial statement tax provision and support U.S. federal, state, and U.S. International tax compliance.

The Senior Manager, Tax Reporting will report to the Tax Associate Director and will focus on two core areas: ASC 740 and U.S. International tax provision and compliance. This role will serve as a technical resource for ASC 740 matters, lead assigned components of the quarterly and annuals income tax provision, and help ensure material tax matters are identified, documented, and reflected accurately in financial reporting deliverables. The role will also review and analyze U.S. International tax provision and compliance matters, including topics such as GILTI, FDII, BEAT, foreign tax credits, Subpart F, Section 986(c), earnings and profits, and related international reporting requirements. This role will also support Domestic tax matters and special projects as needed.

The ideal candidate will have strong tax accounting knowledge, practical experience with U.S. International tax compliance and provision processes, keen analytical skills, and the ability to communicate technical tax concepts clearly to tax and non-tax stakeholders. Experience with OneSource Tax Provision is preferred, and experience with OneSource Income Tax or similar compliance technology is helpful.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead assigned components of the quarterly and annual income tax provision process, including preparation and review of selected provision calculations, journal entries, account analyses, disclosures, and supporting workpapers.
  • Serve as a technical reference point for ASC 740 questions, helping the team research, document, and apply tax accounting guidance to recurring and non-routine matters.
  • Assist with the identification and analysis of material provision items, including uncertain tax positions, valuation allowance considerations, tax law changes, acquisitions and divestitures, audit developments, transfer pricing matters, and tax planning initiatives.
  • Collaborate with the Associate Director of Tax and relevant tax stakeholders to identify, analyze, and appropriately reflect material tax matters within assigned area.
  • Coordinate and support assigned aspects of the international tax provision process, including review and analysis of foreign affiliate tax packages, local provision inputs, deferred tax matters, return-to-provision adjustments, and related documentation.
  • Review and analyze U.S. international tax compliance calculations and reporting, including GILTI, FDII, foreign tax credits, Subpart F, BEAT, Section 986(c), earnings and profits & PTEP.
  • Lead quarterly GILTI deferred tax accounting and reconciliations.
  • Collaborate with Regional Tax, Transfer Pricing, Tax Planning, Tax Audit, Finance, Accounting, Treasury, Legal, and external service providers to understand business transactions and data flows that impact Amgen's provision and tax returns.
  • Prepare and review memoranda or other documentation supporting conclusions for technical tax accounting, U.S. International tax, and non-routine matters.
  • Help maintain SOX-compliant processes and audit-ready workpapers for assigned provision and international tax areas.
  • Identify and implement process improvements, automation opportunities, and control enhancements within assigned provision and international tax workstreams.
  • Provide technical guidance, review comments, training, and day-to-day support to tax professionals on ASC 740 and U.S. International tax matters.
  • Complete special projects and support other Tax Reporting initiatives as needed.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The dynamic professional we seek is a project leader with these qualifications.

  • Doctorate degree and 2 years of analytics experience in Tax Reporting

OR

  • Master’s degree and 4 years of analytics experience in Tax Reporting

OR

  • Bachelor’s degree and 6 years of analytics experience in Tax Reporting

OR

  • Associate’s degree and 10 years of analytics experience in Tax Reporting

OR

  • High school diploma / GED and 12 years of analytics experience in Tax Reporting

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher
  • CPA, MST, JD, LLM, or other relevant advanced tax or accounting credential.
  • 8+ years of tax experience with a strong emphasis on ASC 740 and tax reporting for a large multinational publicly traded company.
  • Public accounting experience preferred
  • Practical experience with both provision and compliance for international tax, including GILTI, FDII, foreign tax credits, Subpart F, Section 986(c), earnings and profits, BEAT, PTEP and Forms 5471, 8858, 8865, 8990, 8991, 8992, 8993.
  • Strong U.S. GAAP background.
  • Experience reviewing or preparing international tax calculations, return-to-provision analyses, deferred tax balances, and audit-ready supporting documentation.
  • Experience with OneSource Tax Provision; experience with OneSource Income Tax, SAP, Alteryx, or other tax technology tools is a plus.
  • Strong research and documentation skills, including the ability to explain technical tax conclusions clearly and concisely.
  • Ability to work in a cross-functional team environment and communicate effectively across multiple levels of management.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage deadlines, competing priorities, and multiple stakeholders during provision and compliance cycles.
  • Proactive ownership, collaborative problem-solving approach, sound judgment, positive attitude, strong work ethic and the ability to operate effectively during time-sensitive reporting cycles
  • Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, or high-tech industry is helpful.

Key Capabilities

  • Technical depth in ASC 740 with the judgment to identify when matters require elevation to the Associate Director or other tax leadership.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. International tax rules and related compliance mechanics, with enough experience to review calculations, ask effective questions, and connect provision impacts to return positions.
  • Translate complex tax concepts into clear implications for Tax Reporting and cross-functional stakeholders, with appropriate escalation to tax leadership.
  • Strong ownership mindset for assigned workstreams, including timely issue identification, clear escalation, and practical recommendations.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, automation, controls, and sustainable tax reporting processes.

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

About Pillar Health Solutions ()

Pillar Health Solutions is a growing healthcare company that partners with medical practices to provide insurance-supported dietary and exercise counseling programs for patients.

Our model connects physicians and their patients with dietitians, virtual trainers, and operational support designed to improve patient engagement and continuity of care.

We are entering an important growth stage and are looking for a Business Development & Operations Lead who can help expand our physician partnerships while strengthening the operational systems and client experience supporting that growth.

This is not a traditional back-office Operations Manager position.

We are looking for someone who can operate as a trusted extension of the leadership team: part business developer, part client success leader, part operator, and part strategic problem solver.

What You Will Own

Physician Acquisition & Business Growth

A major priority for this role is helping Pillar Health Solutions grow its network of physician and medical-practice partners.

You will:

  • Develop and execute practical strategies for attracting new physician and clinic partnerships

  • Identify opportunities to reach physicians, practice owners, office managers, and other healthcare decision-makers

  • Support organic marketing and local-market growth initiatives

  • Help develop physician-facing messaging, success stories, testimonials, and other materials that strengthen Pillar's value proposition

  • Research new channels, tools, partnerships, and approaches for increasing qualified opportunities

You do not need to be a career marketer, but you should understand how businesses grow and be able to contribute thoughtful, executable ideas.

Discovery Calls & Client Conversion

You will help convert interested medical practices into active Pillar partners.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Conducting or facilitating discovery calls with prospective physician partners

  • Explaining Pillar's services and patient-support model confidently

  • Communicating fees, billing structure, workflow, and partnership expectations clearly

  • Understanding the prospective practice's needs and identifying how Pillar can support them

  • Following up on opportunities and moving qualified prospects toward partnership

  • Continuously improving the discovery and conversion process based on feedback and results

Success in this position requires someone who is comfortable speaking directly with physicians, business owners, and senior decision-makers.

Physician, Patient & Program Operations

Once partnerships are established, you will help ensure that the experience remains strong for physicians and patients.

You will:

  • Serve as a key operational contact for physician partners

  • Monitor feedback from physicians and patients and take appropriate action

  • Coordinate with dietitians, virtual trainers, administrative staff, and virtual assistants

  • Support thoughtful matching between patients, dietitians, and virtual trainers when appropriate

  • Monitor patient engagement and identify concerns before they become escalations

  • Address service issues, complaints, and operational breakdowns

  • Help establish appropriate check-ins across the patient, dietitian, trainer, and physician relationship

Because patient experience can directly affect program continuation and business performance, this role requires someone who notices problems early and acts on them.

Founder Partnership & Executive Communication

You will work closely with Pillar Health Solutions leadership and should be comfortable communicating directly with a founder.

Initially, this may include a short daily business update meeting.

You will be expected to:

  • Prepare and drive the agenda rather than waiting for leadership to determine what should be discussed

  • Provide concise updates on projects, priorities, wins, risks, and unresolved issues

  • Explain not only what happened, but why it happened

  • Present recommended next steps and anticipated outcomes

  • Bring thoughtful options instead of open-ended problems

  • Negotiate priorities, expectations, and timelines when necessary

  • Provide respectful pushback when an idea may not be practical or when another priority should come first

  • Maintain transparency even when progress is slower than expected

We are looking for someone who can disagree professionally, communicate difficult information tactfully, and remain levelheaded under pressure.

AI & Technology Integration

Pillar wants AI to become a practical part of how the business operates.

You will:

  • Identify opportunities where AI can improve existing workflows

  • Research tools independently when a business problem arises

  • Use AI for research, analysis, documentation, communication, marketing support, and process improvement

We are looking for practical AI literacy, not simply someone who has used ChatGPT occasionally.

Operational Excellence

Although growth is an immediate priority, you will also help strengthen Pillar's operational foundation.

This may include:

  • Monitoring business and client KPIs

  • Improving workflows as operational gaps become visible

  • Maintaining accurate client, physician, patient, billing, and reporting information

  • Supporting consistent naming conventions and documentation

  • Reviewing processes for accuracy and efficiency

  • Creating or improving SOPs when a documented process is genuinely needed

  • Supporting scheduling, invoicing, reporting, and administrative coordination

  • Helping the company prepare operationally as the number of physician partners and patients increases

As Pillar grows, the scope of the position may expand into greater leadership and team-management responsibilities.

Required Qualifications

  • 2+ years of relevant experience across business operations, executive support, business development, customer success, healthcare operations, or a related field

  • Demonstrated experience working directly with senior leaders, founders, executives, physicians, or business owners

  • Strong client-facing communication and relationship-management skills

  • Ability to manage several responsibilities simultaneously in a startup or rapidly changing environment

  • Experience solving problems independently without waiting for detailed instructions

  • Strong written and verbal communication

  • Confidence facilitating meetings and business conversations

  • Ability to organize information and communicate progress clearly

  • Strong judgment when dealing with sensitive or difficult conversations

  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and processes independently

  • Practical experience using AI tools for business or productivity

  • High attention to detail, particularly where client information, billing, reporting, or financial accuracy is involved

Highly Preferred

  • Healthcare practice, healthcare startup, wellness, medical services, or physician-facing experience

  • Experience supporting a startup founder or small-business owner

  • Experience conducting discovery, sales, partnership, or client-conversion calls

  • Exposure to physician acquisition or healthcare business development

  • Experience with local or organic marketing

jobs.description:
Sunrise,FL - USA

Position Requirements

Location: Remote - nationally deployable; travel to assigned markets as required. This Market Region will cover Central Virginia.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the cadence and accountability infrastructure that keeps NAPA client relationships healthy. Ensure that the right meetings are occurring on schedule, the right stakeholders are in the room, and that no relationship touchpoint falls through the cracks. Track and document all client engagement activity — chief meetings, administrator check-ins, joint reviews — and flag to the RVP when cadence slips or attendance patterns signal disengagement. Maintain timely, accurate records of all client interactions in the CRM. Proactively flag any issue, pattern, or signal that could lead to client dissatisfaction. Prepare materials and briefings that enable executive conversations to be high-quality and well-informed. The CSD will work in partnership with their Operations VP and Clinical VP to determine which relationships will be owned by whom and on what meeting cadence.

  • Serve as the first point of resolution for day-to-day operational issues in assigned markets, including staffing coverage gaps, payroll and scheduling inaccuracies, credentialing coordination, and compliance escalations. Drive accountability across shared services (RCM, HR, Talent Acquisition, Quality) to ensure timely, coordinated responses. Escalate to the RVP on issues determined to be outside of the decision scope.

  • Serve as a visible, accessible advocate for clinicians in assigned markets. Partner with Chiefs and Talent Acquisition on recruitment, onboarding, and credentialing. Monitor engagement signals and address concerns early. Participate in candidate interviewing and provide white-glove onboarding support. Track and address premium pay drivers, vacancy trends, and locum reliance as indicators of cultural or operational breakdown. Maintain knowledge of staffing models and flag model-level risks to the RVP.

  • Provide intentional capacity relief to Regional Vice Presidents by owning the operational and relational layer of account management. Prepare briefing materials, financial summaries, and client meeting prep; attend and support RVP-led strategic engagements as needed. Participate in FORC prep, monthly financial reviews, and other regional initiatives. Identify situations without resolution and bring structured recommendations — not just problem statements — to RVP attention.

  • Actively partner with the RVP to identify and develop expansion opportunities within assigned client accounts. This shall include developing strategic plans for where cross-credentialing should occur to enable more market-based clinical teams. The CSD’s on-the-ground presence and operational relationships make them a primary source of intelligence on client appetite for new service lines, ASC development, volume growth, or contract expansion. Surface these opportunities with specificity — context, timing, and the right internal contact. Maintain awareness of each market’s competitive dynamics and flag threats as well as opportunities. Serve as the connective tissue between field-level insight and NAPA’s RVPs and business development.

SCOPE & DEPLOYMENT MODEL

CSDs are nationally deployable and assigned to markets by need and strategic priority, not by physical proximity alone. A CSD may support multiple markets within a region or cross-region boundaries when RVP capacity and client risk warrant. Assignments are determined collaboratively with Regional SVP leadership and adjusted as portfolio conditions evolve.

Deployment principles:

  • Every client has an assigned, accountable partner with a preset meeting cadence with the executive decision makers for the relationship.

  • Travel cadence is defined by market need; CSDs are expected to achieve meaningful face time with clients and clinicians without being anchored to a single geography.

  • Remote-first work is the operating assumption; on-site presence is purposeful and planned, not incidental.

KEY INTERNAL RELATIONSHIPS

Vice President of Operations - Primary reporting relationship; CSD provides operational and relational capacity relief; escalates only issues requiring RVP authority.

Clinical Vice President - Dotted-line accountability; input on portfolio assignments, performance standards, and strategic priorities.

Chief Physicians / Chief CRNAs - Day-to-day operational partners; CSD supports chief effectiveness and surfaces leadership development needs.

APP Senior Director - Aligned on APP staffing models, performance trends, and practice integration.

Talent Acquisition / HR - Coordinated recruitment, credentialing, onboarding, and provider relations support.

RCM / Accounting - Monitor site-level billing performance; escalate compliance gaps and payer issues.

Client Success / Implementation Teams - Collaboration on new site stand-ups, HyperCare transitions, and escalated client satisfaction situations.

Centralized Scheduling Leadership - High-partnership relationship; CSD owns the effectiveness of every clinical schedule in their market, with shared accountability for delivering consistent operational standards across clients.

Centralized HR Leadership - High-partnership relationship; CSD routes all HR issues — provider relations, payroll concerns, onboarding, credentialing delays, personnel matters — through centralized HR leadership. Acts as the field-level connector and advocate, not the resolver. Timely and accurate escalation to HR is a core performance expectation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field; MBA or equivalent preferred.

  • 5+ years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, account management, or clinical services administration, preferably within an anesthesia or physician practice management organization.

  • Demonstrated track record of managing complex client relationships and driving measurable retention or satisfaction outcomes.

  • Strong financial literacy: ability to read site-level P&Ls, identify performance variances, and communicate financial risk clearly.

  • Experience coordinating clinician recruitment, credentialing, and onboarding workflows in a multi-site healthcare environment.

  • Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to build trust with clinicians, hospital administrators, and executive stakeholders.

  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently — expected 30–50% travel depending on market portfolio.

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience with clinical operations systems including scheduling platforms (Qgenda preferred), practice management tools (iPro preferred), and CRM platforms (Microsoft Dynamics preferred).

  • Experience supporting or leading new site implementations in a healthcare services environment.

  • Familiarity with various types of client contractual agreements.

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED

Client retention in assigned portfolio - No at-risk contracts escalate without early CSD involvement and documented action plan.

RVP capacity relief - RVPs report meaningful reduction in day-to-day operational interruptions from CSD-covered markets.

Issue resolution cycle time - Operational issues are closed at the CSD level; escalation rate to RVP is tracked and declining.

Locum and premium pay reduction - Month-over-month reduction in locum reliance and unplanned premium pay in assigned markets.

Clinician satisfaction / retention - Chiefs and clinicians in CSD-supported markets report accessible, responsive support.

Client relationship health - Regular cadenced client touchpoints are documented; no significant satisfaction deterioration goes unreported.

TOTAL REWARDS:

North American Partners in Anesthesia (NAPA) offers excellent salary, benefits and paid time off.

  • Generous benefits package, including:

    • Paid Time Off

    • Health, life, vision, dental, disability, and AD&D insurance

    • Flexible Spending Accounts/Health Savings Accounts

    • 401(k)

    • Leadership and professional development opportunities

The Clinical Services Director (CSD) is a senior field-facing role responsible for the operational and financial health, clinician experience, and client relationships across an assigned portfolio of NAPA markets. Operating without a geographic residency requirement, the CSD is deployed where need and opportunity are greatest — providing consistent, high-quality support to their markets and amplifying the capacity and effectiveness of their VP of Operations who carries ultimate portfolio accountability.

The CSD role has full P&L ownership for their market and serves as the trusted, accountable partner to both NAPA clients and the clinicians who serve them. This is an intentionally matrixed role. The CSD works within the dyad clinical and operational leadership of their region, and is also expected to work through centralized service delivery leadership to achieve great outcomes. They consistently model the kind of cross-functional partnering that produces repeatable, high-quality output across every market they support.

Campaign Director

Summary:
This position is charged with the authority and responsibility to see that the Campaign vision is developed, managed and successfully funded through vision-donor partnerships.

Essential Duties:
A. Case Development

  • Ensure the campaign case is complete and includes all key components, especially the budget section and the gift plan.
  • Invite the Young Life Communications department to bid on case material.
  • Include a planned giving goal.
  • Ensure that all presentation tools for funding the campaign flow from the case statement and are personalized to target constituencies (e.g. individuals and families, foundations/corporations, churches, etc.).

B. Funding Campaign Operations

  • Ensure that a campaign budget is developed and includes the cost of development, communication and data management and is approved by the Chief Development Officer (CDO).
  • Include a Development Cost Recovery (DCR) factor of 12% (6.5% for campaign and 5.5% for Development department).
  • Place any excess revenue for campaign operations in an account for ongoing fund development work at the camp.

C. Campaign Management

  • Oversee a feasibility study to determine the financial goal for the campaign.
  • Ensure strategies for donors in the software are kept current.
  • On an ongoing basis, clarify in the software what the next step is, who is responsible, when it will take place and how it will be reported.
  • Work with the primary caller, field staff and other campaign directors to assess whether donors have other Young Life interests in order to ensure a seamless and coordinated approach with every major donor (15k and up).
  • Set the timetable for the campaign and the monthly targets to be met to reach the goal.
  • In terms of accountability for the campaign, decision-making is always the campaign director’s (CD) responsibility, and the CDO is responsible for supporting the CD to make sure tasks are completed on time and reported to the appropriate staff and/or volunteers.

D. Ongoing Responsibilities

  • Develop prospects and when appropriate act as a primary caller or a secondary caller available to participate in donor solicitation meetings.
  • Participate in the recruiting of the needed committees and volunteer positions. Lead, train, supervise, support, sustain and thank this staff so that they succeed in their work.
  • A volunteer Executive Committee led by a chair to raise major gifts ($50K and higher)

  • Coordinate campaign activities with other Young Life development entities (e.g. area and regional fundraising efforts, other development initiatives, etc.).
  • Submit the updated database to the CDO monthly.
  • Submit the updated campaign timetable to the CDO monthly.
  • Submit the database prospect report to the CDO in June to support the goal for following fiscal year.
  • Work closely with the executive assistant to the CDO for any assistance and to keep the CDO apprised of all campaign developments and issues in a timely fashion.
  • Establish the campaign office and systems to support campaign operations.

E. Procedures and Policies

  • Camp campaigns can take a DCR on in-kind gifts that replace budgeted items; (there is no DCR for the Service Center).

  • Fund-raised construction policy.
  • Policy on written pledges.

BA degree preferred.

jobs.excerpt: Space Inch is seeking a Director of Engineering to lead our engineering function within a long-standing partnership with one of the largest investment managers in the U.
jobs.description:
Space Inch is seeking a Director of Engineering to lead our engineering function within a long-standing partnership with one of the largest investment managers in the U.S. Partnering closely with our CTO, you'll be the most senior engineering leader on the account: owning day-to-day operational and people leadership, serving as the senior engineering point of contact for the client's stakeholders, and driving AI adoption across the team. This client operates in a highly regulated environment with work spanning many technical stacks, so we want someone who thrives in that variety and brings real operational excellence and care for engineers to an agency environment.

This is first and foremost a people-leadership and communication role. We're looking for an exceptional communicator who earns the trust of engineers and senior client stakeholders alike. You must come from an engineering background, current or former, but hands-on technical depth isn't the primary requirement.

We're also still building out this account's leadership structure, so there's no layer of Engineering Managers under this role yet. You'll lead individual contributors and team leads directly and stay hands-on with delivery yourself, at least for now, with the opportunity to develop engineers on your team into Engineering Managers over time.

Our Mission, Vision, and Values

At Space Inch, we prioritize alignment with our clients and team, ensuring a deep understanding of their needs. We are committed to delivering exceptional work while supporting the personal and professional growth of our team members.

Working at Space Inch

  • Our remote-first team of around 80+ people is based across the EU (mostly Croatia), the US, and Latin America, with a growing presence in Brazil.
  • Occasional travel for client visits and company retreats.
  • This role is embedded within a single long-standing client partnership, though you'll draw on Space Inch's broader engineering community and practices.
  • We support work/life balance for our team.

Requirements

  • 10+ years in software development, with at least 5+ leading engineering teams, including technical delivery leadership (ideally in an agency, consultancy, or client-embedded environment). Distributed team experience is a plus.
  • Exceptional communicator and mediator who bridges client demands with team reality, builds real trust with engineers, and handles sensitive topics (compensation, retention, disengagement, underperformance) directly and with care. Strong across written, async, live, and cross-cultural communication
  • Proactive problem solver who spots delivery, scope, budget, and process breakdowns early (from PTO coverage gaps to missing test data) and fixes them without waiting for permission
  • Hands-on, demonstrable fluency with AI as a working tool: You've personally driven AI adoption in an engineering team with measurable outcomes (tooling rolled out, productivity gains, initiatives delivered); your credibility comes from execution, not commentary
  • Enough technical fluency across modern architecture, SDLC, and common stacks (e.g., React, Vue, Angular, Node.js, Python, Java, C#) to challenge assumptions, guide decisions, and turn vague client requests into execution plans alongside tech leads. You don't need to write production code
  • Experience coordinating multiple teams or workstreams in parallel, with strong stakeholder management on ambiguous or contentious topics, plus staffing, onboarding, interviewing, and resource planning
  • Strong commercial sensibility: translating technical work, operational fixes, and AI-driven gains into a value story clients understand and continue to invest in
  • A systems thinker: organized enough to hold many threads, decisive enough to act without waiting for permission, self-aware enough to loop in leadership after. Experience with internal developer platforms, MCP-style tooling, or prototype-to-production workflows is a plus

Key Responsibilities

  • People leadership, coaching, and retention: Build trust with engineers through regular 1:1s, candid feedback, and development support. Handle sensitive topics directly (compensation, disengagement, underperformance, burnout, departures) and resolve retention risks before they escalate.
  • Client stakeholder management and partnership: Be the senior point of contact for the client, building trust with senior stakeholders, managing shifting priorities, and turning ambiguous requests (a prototype, an HTML mockup, a new app idea) into practical execution plans.
  • Technical program coordination: Coordinate delivery across frontend, backend, DevOps, platform, and tooling workstreams; clarify ownership, align dependencies, and bridge communication gaps between internal teams and the client. Partner with tech leads on architecture and trade-offs.
  • Resourcing and operational ownership: Oversee hiring, onboarding, and staffing; keep engineers productive through client delays; spot and fix delivery, budget, and process breakdowns before they reach the client.
  • AI-driven team uplift: Lead a step-change in how the team uses AI (tooling, upskilling, workflow design) with standards tied to seniority and autonomy. Focus on measurable productivity and code-review quality, not adoption for its own sake.
  • Decisive action and commercial storytelling: Propose and execute fixes without waiting for permission, keeping the CTO informed of what you're doing and why. Translate delivery metrics, technical decisions, and AI gains into a value narrative for the client.

Typical Challenges You'll Be Solving

  • AI adoption that produces measurable outcomes, focused on actual productivity, code review quality, and autonomy.
  • Turning ambiguous client requests into execution plans across multiple workstreams.
  • Maintaining team morale and stability: keeping engineers motivated, engaged, and retention risk low through shifting client priorities, scope changes, or client access delays.
  • Creating clarity in messy space: stepping into situations where domain ownership is unclear, bridging fragmented cross-team conversations, and making sure everyone understands what needs to be done.
  • Balancing short-term delivery needs with longer-term team and technical health.

Qualities for Success

  • Exceptional communicator: empathetic, honest, and transparent. Engineers trust your guidance, feel supported in 1:1s, and follow your lead when priorities shift.
  • Credible in AI as a working tool, with practical experience to back it up.
  • A systems thinker who designs how work happens, quickly spots broken communication loops or process gaps, and fixes them before they escalate.
  • Comfortable making decisions and owning the outcome, even when the first attempt fails.
  • Adapts communication style across coaching, escalation, and client conversations.
  • Calm under client pressure, and doesn't pass that pressure to the team.

The Role Is Right for You If

  • You lead through trust, presence, and communication as much as technical depth, and you're just as comfortable mediating and coaching as you are talking architecture.
  • You're comfortable staying hands-on with delivery and team leadership while this account's structure is still being built out, rather than expecting a team of managers already in place.
  • You see leading AI adoption as one of the most important things a senior engineering leader can do right now, and you want to help engineers navigate a profession that's changing under their feet.
  • You enjoy turning ambiguity into action: spotting what isn't working, proposing a path, and trying it.
  • You're at home in messy situations between people, delivery, client communication, and operations, and take ownership without being asked.

The Role Is Not Right for You If

  • You want a primarily hands-on coding role.
  • You'd rather lead through technical authority than through relationships, trust, and communication.
  • You're looking for a role where a layer of managers already reports to you: that structure doesn't exist yet on this account.
  • You prefer leading through process and approval rather than presence and initiative.
  • You'd rather wait for direction than propose a way forward.

What's In It for You

  • Shape how AI shows up in this account's delivery: visible, measurable, tied directly to client value.
  • Partner with the CTO on engineering at scale.
  • Work across a range of high-impact initiatives within a long-standing client partnership.
  • Remote-friendly, collaborative, pragmatic culture.
  • Leadership team that values people-first thinking and technical excellence.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Monthly salary: $10,000-$13,000 for a full-time B2B collaboration (with flexibility for an exceptional candidate), based on experience and skills
  • Remote-first setup
  • Health & Wellbeing: PTO + 100% Paid sick leave + Annual health checkup
  • Stay active: Wellness subsidy
  • Continuous Growth: An education budget specifically designed to fuel your learning and help you expand your knowledge base.

Space Inch is not responsible for any job boards scraping this ad without showing the position as remote, but Brazil exclusive. Applicants from other countries will not be considered.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

This commitment extends to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, compensation, benefits, and termination. Build Strategic Narratives & Solutions

Location

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. The Opportunity

Cloud spend is no longer just AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Our customers now run a large and growing share of their technology spend through SaaS platforms, data clouds and AI vendors - and every one of those vendors is an integration that brings another slice of their spend into view.

You'll own DoiT's Integrations Framework and the experience built on top of it. This is a chance to define what a great integration experience looks like: a customer connects a new vendor in minutes, sees at a glance that their data is flowing, and handles credential rotation, reconnects and backfills themselves without thinking twice. On the framework side, you'll make adding the next vendor a small, well-understood piece of work rather than a project - so coverage grows as fast as the vendor landscape does.

You'll work AI-augmented from day one. Integration development is spec-driven work against constantly changing third-party APIs: one of the highest-leverage places to apply agentic AI tooling. We expect you to use it across your whole workflow and to have real opinions about where it earns its place.

Responsibilities

  • Building new integrations. This is the core of the role. At Danaher, our work saves lives. And each of us plays a part. Fueled by our culture of continuous improvement, we turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

The Manufacturing IT/OT Security leader is responsible for setting and owning the enterprise operational technology (OT) security strategy for Danaher's global manufacturing portfolio. Operating as both a business and technology leader, this role advances best practices in manufacturing plant security across 15+ operating companies — partnering with global security functions, CIOs, and technology teams to drive control capabilities into the manufacturing environment. The role provides senior technical leadership to a team of engineering leads and holds final approval authority for major architecture decisions in one of the most complex industrial cybersecurity programs in the global life sciences sector.

This position reports to the Senior Director, Cyber Strategy and Enterprise Identity and is part of the Information and Cyber Security organization and will be fully remote.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

  • Lead and advance OT security best practices across the manufacturing portfolio, including IT/OT segmentation, micro segmentation, asset inventory, continuous monitoring, and remote access controls, driving overall program maturity and resilience.

  • Own the OT security strategy, architecture, and platform roadmap, prioritizing and sequencing capability delivery across segmentation, monitoring, asset visibility, and related technologies, with final approval authority for major architecture decisions and associated risk acceptance.

  • Partner with global security functions, CIOs, and operating company technology teams to align enterprise security priorities with operating company execution and embed security controls into manufacturing environments.

  • Establish and govern OT security standards and program effectiveness by authoring enterprise policies, standards, and technical guidance; providing technical oversight to engineering and platform teams; and conducting security assessments against established OT security frameworks to identify and remediate control gaps.

  • Maintain awareness of manufacturing-focused cyber threats and emerging adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), translating threat intelligence and risk insights into defensive priorities, control enhancements, and investment decisions.

The essential requirements of the job include:

  • 15+ years of experience in OT/industrial control system (ICS) security, industrial network engineering, or manufacturing cybersecurity, including establishing technical strategy, governance, and security programs across multi-site industrial environments.

  • Proven ability to operate as both a business and technology leader, partnering with CIOs, global security functions, and technology teams to advance security capabilities and drive adoption across manufacturing operations.

  • Deep expertise in OT security architecture and manufacturing security best practices, including IT/OT segmentation, micro segmentation, asset inventory, monitoring, Purdue Model/ISA-95 zone concepts, industrial DMZ design, IT/OT boundary controls, and hands-on experience with OT security technologies for segmentation, asset visibility, and monitoring.

  • Strong knowledge of OT/ICS environments and cybersecurity frameworks, including experience assessing industrial and manufacturing sites against IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82, ISA-99, and CISA/NSA OT security guidance, with working knowledge of PLCs, DCS, SCADA, HMIs, historians, building management systems, OT protocols, and associated network dependencies.

  • Experience authoring and implementing OT security policies, standards, and technical guidelines across enterprise-scale industrial organizations, coupled with a strong understanding of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) targeting manufacturing and industrial environments.

Position Type: Full-Time
Location: Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Mountain Time

About the Role:

We’re looking for an experienced Account Manager to manage a portfolio of local business clients and help them improve their online visibility and performance.

In this role, you’ll be responsible for building strong client relationships, managing and optimizing Google Business Profiles, monitoring local SEO performance, reviewing analytics, and turning data into clear recommendations. You’ll also use AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to streamline research and content creation while applying your own judgment to ensure the final work is accurate, useful, and aligned with each client’s brand.

The ideal candidate is proactive, organized, comfortable working independently, and able to communicate digital marketing insights clearly to non-technical clients.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for a portfolio of local business clients.
  • Build strong client relationships through consistent communication and proactive updates.
  • Understand each client’s goals, priorities, and business needs.
  • Keep clients informed about progress, results, opportunities, and potential issues.
  • Manage accounts end-to-end and follow through on client commitments.

Local SEO Strategy & Execution

  • Manage and optimize Google Business Profiles for local business clients.
  • Monitor local search rankings and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Manage reviews and support accurate local business information and listings.
  • Implement on-page and off-page SEO strategies tailored to local markets.
  • Identify performance trends, ranking changes, and areas requiring attention.
  • Recommend practical SEO improvements based on client goals and performance data.

Performance Reporting & Analytics

  • Use Google Search Console to monitor search performance, rankings, and potential issues.
  • Use Google Analytics to analyze website and user performance.
  • Interpret marketing data and identify meaningful trends and insights.
  • Prepare clear, actionable performance reports for clients.
  • Explain SEO and analytics results in a simple, easy-to-understand way for non-technical clients.
  • Use reporting insights to guide recommendations and account strategy.

AI-Assisted Workflow

  • Use Claude and ChatGPT to support content creation, research, analysis, and day-to-day deliverables.
  • Use AI tools to improve efficiency and streamline repetitive workflows.
  • Review, edit, and fact-check AI-generated content before delivering it to clients.
  • Ensure AI-assisted outputs meet quality, accuracy, brand, and client-specific standards.
  • Know when AI output needs significant rewriting or should not be used.

Issue Resolution & Escalation

  • Monitor client accounts and identify performance dips or potential issues early.
  • Investigate problems and determine appropriate next steps.
  • Coordinate with internal teams to resolve client issues.
  • Communicate proactively with clients when issues arise.
  • Escalate concerns when necessary, with clear context and recommended solutions.

Growth & Upsell Opportunities

  • Identify opportunities where additional services could benefit clients.
  • Recognize when services such as Google Ads may support a client's goals.
  • Communicate recommendations clearly and professionally without being overly sales-focused.
  • Work with the appropriate internal team when an additional service is identified.

Required Experience & Skills:

  • 2+ years of experience in digital marketing, account management, or a related role.
  • Experience working with local businesses or small-to-medium-sized businesses is strongly preferred.
  • Hands-on experience managing and optimizing Google Business Profiles.
  • Experience with Google Business Profile review management and local listing accuracy.
  • Working knowledge of Google Search Console and Google Analytics.
  • Ability to interpret marketing data and explain findings to non-technical clients.
  • Professional experience using AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT.
  • Strong editorial judgment and ability to review and improve AI-generated content.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Excellent organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple client accounts and priorities independently.
  • Strong problem-solving and follow-through skills.
  • Availability to work full-time during U.S. Mountain Time hours.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Google Ads.
  • Experience managing multiple local SEO accounts simultaneously.
  • Experience working with local service businesses or other location-based businesses.
  • Familiarity with additional SEO, analytics, reporting, or marketing platforms.
  • Experience identifying opportunities for account growth or additional services.

Typical Day:

Your day will balance proactive account management, local SEO work, client communication, and performance analysis.

You may start by reviewing client messages and identifying anything that requires immediate attention. You’ll then work on tasks such as optimizing Google Business Profiles, reviewing Google Search Console for ranking or search-performance changes, analyzing Google Analytics data, and preparing client reports.

You’ll also use Claude or ChatGPT to assist with research and content-related tasks, while reviewing and refining the output before it is delivered. Throughout the day, you’ll communicate with clients, provide updates, address issues, coordinate with internal teams, and identify opportunities to improve account performance or introduce additional services where appropriate.

Job Description Summary

Are you a critical thinker who can analyze complex risk and find insurance solutions that balance customer needs with business goals? If you can take initiative, use both your analytical and creative abilities to make sound decisions and have a desire to help people solve real challenges, we want to hear from you!

Our Excess & Surplus/Specialty (E&S/S) lines allow us to provide insurance that other carriers may not offer. It’s a fast-paced environment in a collaborative, team-oriented culture, working in an always-changing, growing industry.

As an Underwriting Specialist in Brokerage Excess you determine individual risk acceptability, pricing, coverage, terms and conditions, by developing, analyzing and evaluating information and exposures on risks of a complex technical nature for the Excess Casualty line of business. In addition, you’ll achieve production and loss ratio goals with assigned brokers or program managers by reviewing and analyzing claims, loss history and taking appropriate action on accounts. Broker assignments are more complex in terms of coverage and broker relationships. You will work independently with a high level of authority and judgment. Determining appropriate reinsurance placement, if any, on individual accounts is an important element of this role. We will count on you to foster positive business relationships with co-workers, brokers and reinsurers. You will also assist with research, development and presentation of new products, forms and manuals and have opportunities to assist in the training and mentoring of Underwriters and Underwriting Assistants.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • In partnership with Consultant/Manager researches market trends, competition and market viability as well as develops an active working partnership with Actuarial, Finance and Claims as appropriate.

  • Reviews individual risks with assigned brokers and either declines or accepts business based upon information necessary to make the decision. The underwriter analyzes, with a high level of technical expertise, exposures to loss, develops an adequate premium charge for the exposure, determines appropriate endorsements and exclusions to address loss exposures for the insurance contract. Within department guidelines, places reinsurance, if any, for the account.

  • Achieves team/individual production and loss ratio goals with assigned brokers through sound management and marketing. Works with more complex issues concerning coverage. The underwriter continually analyzes premium and loss results of assigned brokers by agency, state, major class of business, etc. Continually assess quality of broker submissions and makes corrective action recommendations.

  • Handles policy maintenance items and other mid-term requests. Reviews endorsement requests and processes necessary changes to the policy. Reviews loss control reports and makes recommendations to the broker and/or changes to the policy. Follows up on outstanding information as required. Reviews claim activity and takes appropriate action.

  • Places reinsurance per department guidelines based upon the appropriate use of all reinsurance facilities used by the department, including various treaty, semiautomatic and facultative reinsurance. Maintains good working relationship with re-insurers.

  • Fosters positive business relationships with brokers, through frequent contact. Develops and maintains good rapport and resolves broker conflicts. Travels to broker offices as required for training or marketing visits. Entertains brokers visiting the Company as required. Assists with development of marketing ideas and strategies for underwriting events and other marketing campaigns.

  • Proactively develops technical and business knowledge through internal and external venues.

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to Underwriting Manager. No direct reports. Indirect reports not typically assigned.

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate degree preferred. Equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

License/Certification/Designation: Completion of general insurance courses such as CPCU, CIC, AU, ARM, CPIW, CWIS, or ASLI is preferred.

Experience: Five years as a CL underwriter, excess & surplus lines experience preferred.

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Knowledge of CL underwriting policies, practices and procedures, insurance law and underwriting marketing principles and techniques. Knowledge of Rating plans and plan concepts. Knowledge of Treaty & Cultivate reinsurance concepts. Knowledge of the wholesale broker system and company operations. Knowledge of regulatory issues, the general agency system, market conditions and company operations. Ability to communicate effectively, verbally, and in writing, inter personally with individuals and groups via telephone, video conference fax, e-mail and in person. Demonstrates negotiation skills. Ability to manage the assigned line or lines of business, which may include monitoring of aggregates. Ability to analyze insurance risks to determine acceptability including policy language, various commercial rating plans and methodologies, reinsurance. Ability to use/learn job related computer software. Ability to devise business solutions to problems, implement the most appropriate, and monitor its effectiveness. Ability to make decisions with minimal supervision.

When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Strategic Segment Manager - Materials, Polymers & Chemicals


Location(s)

High Wycombe, United Kingdom - Remote

Job Description

The Company

PerkinElmer is a global analytical services and solutions provider with offerings including the leading OneSource Field and Laboratory services business that serve the biopharma, food, environmental, safety and applied end markets to accelerate scientific outcomes. Since 1937, PerkinElmer has served as a trusted partner in laboratory analysis and management and today complements its service offerings with a broad portfolio of atomic spectroscopy, molecular spectroscopy, and chromatography instruments, consumables, and reagents. With a dedicated team of more than 5,000 team members, the Company serves customers in more than 35 countries. Additional information is available at www.perkinelmer.com

Purpose

PerkinElmer is seeking a Strategic Segment Manager to own the full go-to-market strategy for Materials, Polymers & Chemicals. This is a market-facing, intelligence-led role that sits at the intersection of product strategy and commercial execution.

The Strategic Segment Manager is the organisation's foremost expert on their assigned market: the customer workflows, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and purchasing patterns that determine how PerkinElmer wins or loses in that segment. They translate this expertise into Market Requirements Documents that shape product roadmaps, go-to-market playbooks that guide commercial execution, and value propositions that give the sales organisation a compelling story to tell.

This is a cross-product-line role. The Strategic Segment Manager sees the segment horizontally — understanding how customers in their market use the full range of PerkinElmer's analytical capabilities, and identifying where the portfolio wins, where it loses, and where it needs to evolve.

Responsibilities:

Market Intelligence & VOC

  • Maintain deep, current knowledge of the assigned segment: customer workflows, buying behaviour, regulatory and compliance requirements, competitive landscape, and technology adoption trends
  • Execute a structured VOC program, covering current users, competitive users, and prospective customers across the segment's key geographies and sub-verticals
  • Build and maintain relationships with key opinion leaders, industry associations, regulatory bodies, and academic partners in the segment — establishing PerkinElmer as a credible, trusted partner in the relevant scientific community
  • Conduct systematic competitive intelligence: tracking competitor product launches, pricing, application claims, and go-to-market moves — translating intelligence into actionable competitive response recommendations

Market Requirements Documents (MRDs)

  • Own the segment's Market Requirements Document — the structured, evidence-based articulation of customer needs, competitive gaps, and product investment priorities for the assigned segment across all relevant PerkinElmer product lines
  • Update and maintain the MRD on a structured annual cadence, with interim updates when significant market events (competitive launches, regulatory changes, customer feedback patterns) require immediate revision
  • Present MRD findings and recommendations to the VP Product Line teams, VP Marketing, and Sr. Director — defending investment priorities with customer evidence and commercial data, not assumption
  • Ensure MRD inputs are formally adopted into at least one VP Product Line roadmap planning cycle per year, tracking implementation of MRD-driven product decisions

Go-to-Market Strategy & Commercial Enablement

  • Develop the segment go-to-market strategy: target customer profiles, channel priorities, campaign themes, value proposition hierarchy, and commercial messaging that positions PerkinElmer's portfolio competitively in the assigned segment
  • Produce commercially actionable segment enablement tools: competitive battlecards, segment application guides, customer workflow maps, and sales playbooks that Regional Marketing Managers and the field sales organisation can deploy immediately
  • Partner with the Portfolio marketing team to brief and review segment-specific campaign content — ensuring technical accuracy, commercial relevance, and strategic alignment with the segment's priority themes
  • Drive annual growth planning for the assigned segment — identifying the highest-priority growth initiatives, the product line actions required to capture them, and the commercial resources needed to win

Thought Leadership & External Presence

  • Develop segment-specific thought leadership content: white papers, application note series themes, scientific conference presentations, and regulatory commentary that establishes PerkinElmer as a knowledgeable, credible voice in the segment
  • Represent PerkinElmer at segment-specific conferences, trade shows, and customer advisory events — speaking, networking, and gathering market intelligence
  • Contribute to PerkinElmer's customer advisory board programming for the segment — designing agendas, facilitating discussions, and translating advisory input into commercial and product management action

Success Metrics

  • MRD completion and adoption — annual MRD delivered on schedule and formally adopted in at least one VP Product Line roadmap planning cycle
  • VOC coverage — minimum 25 documented in-depth customer conversations per year
  • Segment growth contribution — revenue growth in the assigned segment vs. prior year and vs. market growth rate
  • Enablement asset quality and utilization — Portfolio marketing content briefed, commercial tools produced, and field adoption rate of segment playbooks and battlecards
  • Competitive win rate in the segment — tracked through win/loss analysis

Qualifications & Experience:

Required

  • 8+ years of experience in product management, segment marketing, market intelligence, or applications science within analytical instrumentation, life sciences tools, or a closely adjacent scientific or industrial technology business
  • Deep domain expertise in the assigned segment — sufficient to engage credibly with customer scientists, interpret regulatory requirements, and identify commercially significant technical developments without specialist support
  • Demonstrated experience conducting structured VOC programmes and translating customer insight into rigorous, commercially actionable product strategy inputs
  • Experience producing strategic documents — Market Requirements Documents, market assessments, or competitive analyses — used to drive product investment decisions
  • Strong communication skills: able to write and present at a high standard for both technical and commercial audiences
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline

Preferred

  • Advanced degree (MSc, PhD) providing peer-level scientific credibility with customers and with the product line PM teams the Segment Manager must influence
  • Experience working in the assigned segment — as a researcher, analytical chemist, regulatory specialist, or applications expert — giving first-hand understanding of customer workflows and decision drivers
  • Track record of external scientific engagement: publications, conference presentations, or regulatory body participation in the assigned market
  • Experience building competitive intelligence systems or structured VOC programmes where none previously existed

Job Requisition ID #


26WD100980

Autodesk Fusion is is redefining how products get designed and made, bringing CAD, CAM, CAE, and PCB together on one cloud platform at a price point that puts professional tools within reach of every engineer and every shop. That self-serve motion is a massive advantage in EMEA, where the market is defined by its long tail: hundreds of thousands of small design studios and machine shops that discover, evaluate, and adopt tools digitally. This role exists to own the EMEA growth engine, finding the channels that work country by country, converting trials into subscribers, and proving with data where the next investment should go.

What you'll do

  • Own the EMEA acquisition and conversion funnel end-to-end: traffic → signup → trial activation → paid subscription → expansion — with revenue targets, not just lead targets

  • Champion and sharpen Fusion's PLG motion in EMEA: optimize the self-serve journey so the product sells itself — frictionless trials, activation moments that show value fast, and upgrade paths that feel natural

  • Partner with the Performance Marketing team to get the right channel in front of the right audience — bringing regional audience insight, conversion data, and funnel priorities that shape where and how paid investment lands in each market

  • Drive localization that converts, not just translates: landing pages, onboarding flows, and campaign creative adapted for priority markets (Germany, UK, France, Italy, Nordics), informed by conversion data per market

  • Partner with PMM, Campaigns, and Demand Gen to run growth experiments across digital, email, and in-product — a constant cadence of tests with clear hypotheses, measured results, and shared learnings that compound across teams

  • Build measurement frameworks with analytics that attribute performance through to signups, activations, and subscription revenue by market — and report clearly on what's working, what isn't, and what you're changing

Who you are

  • 5–8+ years in growth marketing, or growth PMM at a B2B SaaS or PLG company; you've owned a self-serve funnel with revenue accountability

  • Hands-on, not just a briefer: you've built campaigns, written conversion copy, set up experiments, and lived in dashboards yourself

  • Analytically rigorous: comfortable designing experiments, reading incrementality, and defending a budget reallocation with data

  • Fluent in EMEA growth mechanics: you understand how channel mix, CPCs, privacy regulation (GDPR/ePrivacy), and buying behavior vary across European markets, and you've marketed in more than one of them (English required; German preferred)

  • A strong cross-functional operator who can be the connective tissue between product, PMM, lifecycle, and paid teams

  • Curious about our users: you want to understand why a machinist in Bavaria or a design studio in Milan does or doesn't convert, and you'll go find out

The ideal candidate

  • Has built growth workflows with AI beyond the chat window. You've stood up repeatable systems, automated creative variant generation and testing, AI-driven audience or funnel analysis, localized copy pipelines, churn-signal monitoring and can show what you built and what it changed

  • Has scaled a market that wasn't working. You've taken a region or channel that was underperforming, diagnosed why, and turned it into a growth driver, not just optimized something already scaling

  • Knows how to turn product releases into acquisition moments. You've partnered with PMM to convert launch attention into signups and trials, not just traffic spikes

Who this role is not for

  • If you need someone else to pull the data. You'll live in dashboards and build your own analysis; waiting on an analyst for every question will slow you to a halt

  • If you only know one playbook. What worked at your last company won't transplant cleanly across five European markets, you'll be testing your way to the answer

  • If "awareness" is your success metric. Everything here ties to signups, activation, and subscription revenue; if you can't connect your work to those numbers, this will be uncomfortable

How we'll measure success

  • EMEA funnel performance: signups, trial-to-paid conversion, and subscription revenue growth by market

  • Experiment velocity and learning: a steady cadence of tests with results that change how we invest

  • Quality of partnership: PMM, Campaigns, and global Growth would name you as the person who made EMEA legible

About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

About the role

We are seeking an experienced and proactive Major Case Claims Resolution Specialist to oversee high-exposure, complex, and litigated claims involving serious injuries In this role, you will take ownership of the full claims lifecycle—from initial investigation through resolution—while managing litigation strategy and collaborating with defense counsel.

You’ll be a key point of contact for all stakeholders, including claimants, legal counsel, medical professionals, and internal teams. These files often involve layered policies, multi-party litigation, and sensitive negotiation. You will be empowered to shape case strategy, resolve complex coverage issues, and maintain a strong focus on timely, thoughtful outcomes.

This role also includes the opportunity to influence how we streamline and improve our processes by working closely with our product and engineering teams to deliver feedback from the frontlines of complex claim handling.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

What you'll do

  • Managing all aspects of litigated cases, including evaluation of the resolution process
  • Analyze auto claims to identify areas of dispute, investigating and gathering all necessary information and documentation, evaluating liability and damages and negotiating and resolving claims with opposing parties or their insurance providers
  • Manage litigation cases related to auto claims disputes, communicating regularly with clients, attorneys, vendors and other stakeholders
  • Review legal documents and ensuring compliance with initial suit-handling plan of action.
  • Analyze policy language and reaching appropriate coverage decisions.
  • Direct and control the activities and costs of outside vendors including defense counsel and coverage counsel, experts and independent adjusters
  • Maintain the appropriate adjuster licenses and continuing education requirements

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree (lack of one should not stop you from applying if you possess all the other qualifications)
  • 10+ years of claim handling experience, with 5+ of those years handling a pending of >60% in litigation
  • Experience with Commercial Auto is Required
  • You are not intimidated by an attorney, even if you are not one! You are the driver of the litigation strategy for any particular claim. You manage the discovery in the order and timing of events and hold attorney accountable
  • Having an understanding of transportation coverages, contractual risk transfers, and additional insured forms
  • You have strong medical causation knowledge
  • You have a sense of urgency and understanding of how to manage time-sensitive demands
  • Ability and willingness to communicate both on the phone and in written form in a prompt, courteous, and professional manner
  • Strong analytical and negotiation skills. You will conduct your own negotiations directly with opposing counsel
  • Knowledge of multiple state statutes, including good faith claim handling practices, regulations, and guidelines
  • Ability to professionally collaborate with all stakeholders in a claim
  • Active adjuster license: resident-state license where available, otherwise a Designated Home State (DHS) license. Willing to obtain any additional required licenses within 60 days, including state testing.
  • Attention to detail, time management, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, remote environment
  • Curious and motivated by problem solving and questioning the status quo
  • Desire to engage in learning opportunities and continuous professional development
  • Willingness to travel for client and claims needs

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • Work from anywhere to facilitate your work life balance
  • Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder!

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

Job Description

A bit about this role:

Our Eligibility & Enrollment team is the front door to the member experience — we process every enrollment, disenrollment, plan change, and retroactive adjustment across our HMO, PPO, and Special Needs Plan products, and we own the CMS transactions that make membership accurate and auditable. As Manager, you'll turn departmental strategy into daily workflows, production targets, and staff assignments, keeping the work compliant with CMS requirements and on time.

You'll report to the Senior Manager, Eligibility & Enrollment and lead a team of Enrollment/Eligibility Associates. This is a hands-on operational leadership role: you'll be in the queues, in the data, and in the escalations, while building the reporting and controls the team runs on. Your results show up directly in CMS transaction accuracy and timeliness, inventory aging, quality audit scores, and the member experience measures tied to enrollment accuracy.

Your responsibilities and impact will include:

  • Managing daily workflow, work queues, and transaction inventory so enrollments, disenrollments, plan changes, cancellations, and retroactive adjustments across HMO, PPO, and SNP products clear within CMS and internal SLAs, holding aging and backlog inside established thresholds.

  • Monitoring CMS MARx submissions, response and reply files, and error reports so rejections and discrepancies are researched and resolved inside required timeframes, and membership reconciliation lands accurate and on time each month.

  • Serving as the first point of escalation on complex and exception-based cases, making case-level decisions consistent with CMS guidance and internal policy.

  • Supervising, coaching, and developing associates — hiring, onboarding, scheduling, one-on-ones, performance management, and individual production and quality goals tied to department KPIs — and owning the team's productivity, quality, engagement, and retention. You'll set the tone for accountability and service excellence, and address performance or conduct issues promptly and consistently.

  • Planning capacity and coverage for peak cycles, including AEP, OEP, and Special Election Periods, so volume surges don't become backlog.

  • Performing and documenting quality reviews of transactions and member records against the CMS Medicare Managed Care Enrollment and Disenrollment Guidance and internal controls, and driving individual and team audit scores.

  • Supporting CMS, internal, and external audits by preparing universes, pulling case files, validating samples, and answering auditor questions; executing assigned corrective action plans and closing them on time, with no repeat findings in your area.

  • Translating new CMS guidance and memos into operational changes — recommending workflow updates to the Senior Manager, keeping job aids and desk-level procedures current, and training staff on regulatory changes and system enhancements.

  • Identifying recurring errors, rework drivers, and manual workarounds, then implementing process improvements and automation opportunities.

  • Building and maintaining notebooks and monitoring views for volume, aging, throughput, accuracy, timeliness, and reconciliation completion, and escalating trends and risks with a recommended action rather than just a number.

  • Partnering with peer managers and staff on the design and use of AI agents in transaction processing under a human-in-the-loop model: defining where human review is required, setting quality checkpoints on agent-assisted output, documenting controls to audit standards, and coaching the team against over-reliance on automated output.

  • Partnering with Member Services, Billing, Data Reconciliation, Compliance, Sales, Agent Support, and Tech on member-impacting issues, defect resolution, file transmission and interface monitoring, and UAT for configuration changes, upgrades, new products, and plan expansions.

  • Supporting the Senior Manager with materials and analysis for leadership, CMS inquiries, and internal governance forums.

Required skills and experience:

  • 4+ years in Medicare Advantage eligibility and enrollment operations, including at least 2 years in a supervisory or team lead role.

  • Working knowledge of CMS enrollment and disenrollment regulations for HMO, PPO, and SNP products, including election periods, effective dating, and retroactive processing rules.

  • Hands-on experience with CMS MARx transaction processing, response and reply file handling, and membership reconciliation.

  • Experience supporting CMS or internal audits, including universe preparation and case documentation.

  • Strong analytical and root-cause problem-solving skills on complex transaction and eligibility discrepancies, with proficiency in Excel and reporting tools for inventory tracking, trend analysis, and audit sampling.

  • Demonstrated aptitude for hands-on operational tooling — including the ability to learn and build notebooks for metric monitoring and reporting — and willingness to work directly in AI-assisted processes under a human-in-the-loop model.

  • Effective written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain regulatory requirements to staff and non-technical partners.

  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and high-volume workloads in a deadline-driven, regulated environment, with a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy and member confidentiality (HIPAA).

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Health Administration, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and directly relevant Medicare enrollment experience will be considered.

  • Ability to work remotely with availability to support extended coverage during AEP, OEP, and other peak enrollment periods.

Desired skills and experience:

  • Health plan, MSO, or TPA experience, with proficiency in a health plan administration platform (QNXT, Facets, HealthEdge, or similar) and CMS data exchange tools including HPMS.

  • Experience designing or overseeing AI agents in an operational workflow; master's degree (MBA, MHA, or similar)
